full_text_en:
Feng Haojiang et al. v. Dongguan City Planning Bureau of Guangdong Province — Dispute over Administrative Ruling on House Demolition Compensation

Ruling Summary

If the appraisal report relied upon by an administrative authority when making an administrative ruling suffers from serious procedural defects, such as the appraiser lacking statutory appraisal qualifications or the appraiser failing to collect evidence in accordance with the law, it shall be determined that the administrative authority's ruling lacks sufficient primary evidence and shall be revoked according to law.

Plaintiffs: Feng Haojiang et al. (17 persons) (list omitted), all owners of shops at No. 18 Dongzong Avenue, Dongguan City, Guangdong Province.

Litigation Representative: Li Yifan.

Defendant: Dongguan Urban Construction and Planning Bureau of Guangdong Province. Domicile: Dongcheng Zhong Road, Dongguan City, Guangdong Province.

Legal Representative: Zhu Chuan, Director of the Bureau.

Third Party: Dongguan City Urban Area Real Estate Development Company of Guangdong Province. Domicile: Dongcheng West Road, Dongguan City, Guangdong Province.

Legal Representative: Yuan Kong, General Manager of the Company.

Third Parties: Feng Yanfen, Zhou Bingkun, Zhang Ganlin, Liu Fazhi, all owners of shops at No. 18 Dongzong Avenue, Dongguan City, Guangdong Province.

On August 30, 2002, the Dongguan Urban Construction and Planning Bureau of Guangdong Province (hereinafter referred to as the Dongguan Planning Bureau), based on the application of Dongguan City Urban Area Real Estate Development Company (hereinafter referred to as the Development Company), issued the Donggui Xingcai (2002) No. 1 Administrative Ruling on House Demolition (hereinafter referred to as the Demolition Ruling) concerning the demolition and resettlement of 24 privately-owned shops located at No. 18 Dongzong Avenue. The main contents included: (1) Compensation and resettlement for the 24 shops at No. 18 Dongzong Avenue shall be carried out as follows: if the demolished parties choose monetary compensation, the applicant shall pay a lump sum to each demolished party according to the appraisal amount in the demolition appraisal report provided by the applicant; if the demolished parties choose property right exchange, if the exchange is based on a ratio of 1:0.6 between the demolished house area and the new shops on the same site, no compensation difference is required between the parties; if the exchange is based on a ratio of 1:1 between the demolished house area and the new shops on the same site, the parties shall calculate the compensation amount for the demolished house and the price of the exchanged house, and settle the difference in property rights exchange. (2) The applicant shall pay a one-time business loss compensation to the demolished parties, calculated at 80% of the monthly average after-tax profit verified by the tax authority for the six months prior to the announcement of the house demolition, for a period of six months. (3) The applicant shall pay a one-time moving fee of RMB 1,000 per shop to the demolished parties. (4) Compensation for interior decoration shall be provided in accordance with relevant municipal standards. (5) Within fifteen days from the effective date of this ruling, the demolished parties must move out of the 24 shops at No. 18 Dongzong Avenue, and these houses shall be demolished by the applicant. Feng Haojiang and 16 other owners, dissatisfied with the Demolition Ruling, filed an administrative lawsuit with the Dongguan Intermediate People's Court of Guangdong Province.

Plaintiffs' Allegations: The appraisal report relied upon by the defendant in the above ruling was erroneous in its application of law regarding the commissioning entity, conditions and scope of use, and applicable procedures. Moreover, the relevant content of the appraisal report and the identities of the appraisers were not subject to cross-examination by the plaintiffs. The ruling result infringed upon the plaintiffs' lawful rights and interests. The plaintiffs request that the defendant's administrative ruling on house demolition be revoked.

The main evidence provided by the plaintiffs included:
1. The Demolition Ruling made by the Dongguan Planning Bureau and the Hualian Pingzi (2002) No. 25 Appraisal Report (hereinafter referred to as the Appraisal Report) issued by Dongguan Hualian Certified Public Accountants Co., Ltd. of Guangdong Province (hereinafter referred to as Hualian Company), to prove the existence of the specific administrative act being sued.
2. Price lists for the second and third phases of shops at Yonghua Court, to prove that the appraisal price adopted by the Dongguan Planning Bureau in the Appraisal Report was far lower than the price of shops at nearby Yonghua Court.
3. The House Ownership Certificates of Feng Haojiang et al., to prove the area and location of the demolished houses and the nature of the houses as "shops."

Defendant's Defense: The appraisal report relied upon in the ruling was made by Hualian Company, which is an independent enterprise legal person established with approval from the administrative authority for industry and commerce and possesses asset appraisal qualifications approved and issued by the Ministry of Finance. Its asset appraisal scope includes various types of assets such as real estate and machinery equipment. Furthermore, the appraisal report and the qualifications of the appraisal institution were subject to cross-examination by all plaintiffs during the hearing. Therefore, the appraisal report is credible and lawful. Our bureau's administrative ruling procedure was lawful, the application of law was correct, and the plaintiffs' grounds for lawsuit are untenable.

The main evidence provided by the defendant included:
1. The Construction Land Use Planning Permit, the State-owned Land Use Certificate, and the House Demolition Permit, to prove that before applying for the administrative ruling, the Development Company had obtained the land use planning permit, land use certificate, and demolition permit for the location of the property in question.
2. The Hualian Pingzi (2002) No. 25 Appraisal Report made by Hualian Company, to prove the main basis for making the administrative ruling.
3. The Hearing Record of Administrative Ruling prepared by the Dongguan Planning Bureau, to prove that before making the administrative ruling, a public hearing was organized with the plaintiffs and the third parties.

Third Party Development Company's Statement: The plaintiffs' claim that the demolishing party never negotiated with the demolished parties on compensation and resettlement issues is clearly inconsistent with the facts. Our company has already reached house demolition compensation agreements with owners such as Han Liuqiong, Su Weiwen, Zhang Ganlin, Liu Fazhi, and Zhou Bingkun, and has also conducted multiple negotiations with Feng Haojiang et al. on compensation and resettlement issues. The plaintiffs' claim that the price appraisal in the Appraisal Report is manifestly unfair is unsupported by evidence. Our company only needs to prove that Hualian Company, which produced the Appraisal Report, is a lawfully established legal institution with appraisal qualifications. Whether the appraisal report is fair should be determined by legal standards. Therefore, the administrative ruling made by the defendant has clear factual findings, correct application of law, and appropriate ruling content, and should be upheld.

The evidence provided by Third Party Development Company included:
1. Minutes of negotiations between the Development Company's development office and Feng Haojiang et al. on compensation and resettlement issues, to prove that the Development Company had negotiated with Feng Haojiang et al. before applying for the ruling.
2. House Demolition Compensation Agreements reached between the Development Company's development office and Han Liuqiong et al., to prove that the real estate development company had also negotiated with Feng Haojiang et al. before applying for the ruling, and to demonstrate that the compensation standard in the Appraisal Report had been accepted by demolished parties such as Han Liuqiong.

The other third parties in this case did not appear in court to state their opinions.

The Dongguan Intermediate People's Court found the following facts upon trial:

On December 10, 2001, the defendant, the Dongguan Planning Bureau, issued House Demolition Permit No. Chai Xu Zi (2001) No. 5 to the Third Party Development Company, authorizing the Development Company to demolish the 24 shops at No. 18 Dongzong Avenue owned by the 21 persons including the plaintiffs in this case. The compensation plan proposed by the Development Company was: (1) Valuation compensation, with a one-time cash compensation based on the demolished construction area, with the compensation amount calculated according to the appraised value; (2) Property right exchange, exchanging property rights based on a ratio of 1:0.6 between the construction area of the existing shops and the new shops on the same site, with no compensation for the difference. However, after multiple negotiations, the Development Company and the plaintiffs in this case failed to reach a compensation and resettlement agreement for the demolition. In April 2002, the Development Company applied to the Dongguan Planning Bureau for an administrative ruling, naming the plaintiffs in this case, as well as Han Liuqiong, Huang Xuchao, and 21 other persons as the demolished parties. Commissioned by the Development Company, Hualian Company made an asset appraisal report on the shops to be demolished on May 20, 2002. The appraisal conclusion was: the average appraised price for the shops to be demolished was RMB 5,194.61 per square meter, and the average appraised price for the warehouses was RMB 3,480 per square meter. On August 20, 2002, the Dongguan Planning Bureau convened a public hearing for the demolishing party and the demolished parties on the house demolition compensation dispute. On August 30, 2002, the Dongguan Planning Bureau issued the Demolition Ruling.

Opinion of the Dongguan Intermediate People's Court:

Administrative litigation is a review of the legality of the specific administrative act being sued. Therefore, the object of review in this case is whether the ruling made by the defendant was lawful. Article 16 of the Regulations on the Administration of Urban House Demolition provides: "If the demolishing party and the demolished party, or the demolishing party, the demolished party, and the lessee of the house fail to reach a compensation and resettlement agreement, upon application by a party, the house demolition management department shall make a ruling..." Article 23 provides: "Compensation for demolition may be in the form of monetary compensation or property right exchange of houses." Article 24 provides: "The amount of monetary compensation shall be determined based on the market appraisal price of the real estate, taking into account factors such as the location, use, and construction area of the demolished house." Therefore, the Dongguan Planning Bureau had the authority to make a ruling on the Development Company's application. The Dongguan Planning Bureau's ruling was made after a public hearing, with the Appraisal Report as a basis, and the ruling result provided two options—monetary compensation and property right exchange—for the demolished households to choose. Moreover, the amount of monetary compensation was determined based on the market appraisal price of the real estate, which complies with the provisions of the above regulations. It should be determined that the ruling had clear factual findings, correct application of laws and regulations, and was a lawful specific administrative act. Feng Haojiang et al. claimed that the Appraisal Report relied upon by the Dongguan Planning Bureau in its ruling violated Article 18 of the Detailed Rules for the Implementation of the Measures for the Administration of State-owned Assets Valuation in terms of the commissioning entity, conditions and scope of use, and applicable procedures, and that the application of law was erroneous. Since the appraised property in question was privately owned, not state-owned assets, it did not fall within the scope of adjustment of the Detailed Rules for the Implementation of the Measures for the Administration of State-owned Assets Valuation. At the same time, the amount of valuation compensation in the Dongguan Planning Bureau's ruling was determined based on the market appraisal price of the real estate. Therefore, the plaintiffs' ground for action on this point is not supported. Feng Haojiang et al. claimed that the relevant content of the Appraisal Report and the identities of the appraisers relied upon by the Dongguan Planning Bureau in its ruling were not subject to cross-examination by the plaintiffs. Upon investigation, the hearing procedure conducted by the Dongguan Planning Bureau had already conducted a hearing on the relevant evidence, and according to Hualian Company's business license, the firm has asset appraisal qualifications. Feng Haojiang et al. failed to submit evidence to prove that the appraisal report was unlawful or unreliable. The Dongguan Planning Bureau's adoption of this appraisal report as the basis for the ruling was not improper. Feng Haojiang et al. claimed that the appraisal price in the Appraisal Report was far lower than the prices of shops at Jufu Haoyuan, Yonghua Court, and Donghu Garden, and that the appraisal price was manifestly unfair. Upon investigation, the shops in question, aside from their location, are not comparable to shops in Jufu Haoyuan, Yonghua Court, or Donghu Garden on other indicators. Feng Haojiang et al. claimed that the content of the Demolition Ruling exceeded the scope of the Development Company's request and infringed upon the lawful rights and interests of the demolished households. Upon investigation, the Development Company applied for the defendant's ruling because it could not reach a compensation and resettlement agreement with the demolished households. The five items in the Dongguan Planning Bureau's ruling did not exceed the scope of compensation and resettlement for demolition or the scope of the Development Company's request. In summary, the grounds for Feng Haojiang et al. to request revocation of the Demolition Ruling are all untenable and are not supported.

Accordingly, in accordance with Article 56, Item (2) of the Interpretation of the Supreme People's Court on Several Issues Concerning the Implementation of the Administrative Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China, the Dongguan Intermediate People's Court rendered the following judgment on March 28, 2003:

Reject the lawsuit claims of the 17 plaintiffs including Feng Haojiang.

After the first instance judgment was rendered, Feng Haojiang et al. appealed to the Guangdong High People's Court.

Feng Haojiang et al. appealed, claiming: The first instance court's factual findings were unclear. There was no basis for the first instance court's finding that the appellee held a hearing on August 20, 2002. The evidence admitted by the first instance court was unlawful. The Appraisal Report divided the appellants' shops into shops and warehouses, and proposed that "if the property right exchange is based on a ratio of 1:0.6 between the demolished house area and the new shops on the same site, no compensation difference is required between the parties," which was clearly contrary to fairness. Therefore, the appellants requested that the first instance judgment be reversed and the Planning Bureau's administrative ruling be revoked.

The Planning Bureau responded: The first instance court's factual findings were clear. Feng Haojiang et al.'s claim that no hearing procedure was held was inconsistent with the facts. Our bureau only needed to prove that Hualian Company, which produced the Appraisal Report, was a lawfully established legal institution with appraisal qualifications. We have no authority to comment on the specific content of the Appraisal Report. Therefore, Feng Haojiang et al.'s claim that the price appraisal in the Appraisal Report was manifestly unfair was unsupported by evidence.

The Third Party Development Company's response reasons and requests in the second instance were the same as those of the Planning Bureau.

Third Party Feng Yanfen et al. stated in the second instance: They agreed with the opinions of Feng Haojiang et al.

The Guangdong High People's Court found the following facts upon second instance trial: After accepting the Development Company's application, the Dongguan Planning Bureau presided over a public hearing on August 20, 2002, and produced a Hearing Record of Administrative Ruling. The appellants' litigation representative Li Yifan and his agent ad litem signed this record. Moreover, Li Yifan confirmed this during the second instance trial. Therefore, the objection raised by Feng Haojiang et al. that the Dongguan Planning Bureau did not hold a hearing was untenable. Other facts found by the first instance court, to which the parties raised no objections, should be confirmed.

Opinion of the Guangdong High People's Court:

When the Dongguan Planning Bureau adopted the Appraisal Report made by Hualian Company as the basis for its administrative ruling, it should have reviewed matters such as the qualifications of the appraisers who prepared the Appraisal Report and the appraisal procedures. Article 24 of the Interim Provisions on the Professional Qualification System for Registered Asset Appraisers, jointly issued by the Ministry of Personnel and the State Administration of State-owned Assets, provides: "The project leader for an appraisal project undertaken by an asset appraisal institution shall be a registered asset appraiser. An appraisal report shall be signed by at least two registered asset appraisers to be valid." In this case, the appraisers who signed the Appraisal Report were Zhang Ruiming and Xiao Xiaokang. However, only Zhang Ruiming had registered asset appraiser qualifications; Xiao Xiaokang did not. According to the above provision, the Appraisal Report is invalid. The reason the Appraisal Report divided the property in question into shops and warehouses for separate appraisals was that the information provided by the commissioning Development Company had already pre-classified the property into shops and warehouses. Zhang Ruiming, as a registered asset appraiser, failed to review the information provided by the commissioning party, the Development Company, during the appraisal and directly adopted it, which violated Article 18 of the Code of Professional Ethics for Chinese Registered Asset Appraisers issued by the Ministry of Finance: "A registered asset appraiser shall inspect the assets entrusted by the client for appraisal and review the relevant information provided by the client." Moreover, the House Ownership Certificates held by Feng Haojiang et al. recorded the property in question as "shop units." Hualian Company did not provide any evidence or legal basis to prove that "shop units" could be interpreted as shops and warehouses. Therefore, the division of the property into shops and warehouses in the Appraisal Report lacked a basis and could not be relied upon. In addition, Hualian Company stated that the rental standard used in the Appraisal Report was determined by inquiring with relevant persons around the property in question. However, the appraiser Zhang Ruiming was unable to provide evidence to prove this. Therefore, the rental standard adopted by Hualian Company lacked sufficient evidence. Since one of the two appraisers who prepared the Appraisal Report did not have statutory appraisal qualifications, and the appraisers neither reviewed the information provided by the commissioning real estate development company nor lawfully collected evidence to prove the rental standard they adopted, there were serious procedural violations. The Dongguan Planning Bureau, without lawfully reviewing the above matters of the Appraisal Report, adopted it as the basis for its administrative ruling, which should be determined as insufficient evidence for the ruling and should be revoked according to law. Article 62 of the Provisions of the Supreme People's Court on Several Issues Concerning Evidence in Administrative Litigation provides: "Where the defendant has adopted an expert conclusion in an administrative procedure, and the plaintiff or a third party presents evidence proving any of the following circumstances, the people's court shall not adopt the expert conclusion: (1) The expert lacks expert qualifications; (2) The expert procedure is seriously illegal..." Accordingly, the first instance court's adoption of the appraisal conclusion in the Appraisal Report was improper and constituted an error in the application of law. At the same time, the first instance court's use of the Appraisal Report as the basis for determining the lawfulness of the administrative ruling being sued constituted unclear factual findings.

Accordingly, in accordance with Article 61, Item (3) and Article 54, Item (2), Sub-item 1 of the Administrative Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China, the Guangdong High People's Court rendered the following judgment on December 12, 2003:

1. Revoke the first instance administrative judgment of the Dongguan Intermediate People's Court;
2. Revoke the Donggui Xingcai (2002) No. 1 Administrative Ruling on House Demolition of the Dongguan Urban Construction and Planning Bureau of Guangdong Province;
3. The Dongguan Urban Construction and Planning Bureau of Guangdong Province shall make a new ruling within 60 days from the date of receipt of this judgment.
